title: BRAIN INITIATIVE RESOURCE: DEVELOPMENT OF A HUMAN NEUROELECTROMAGNETIC DATA ARCHIVE AND TOOLS RESOURCE (NEMAR)
text:
We propose to continue the development of the NEMAR web portal to neuroelectromagnetic
(NEM) brain imaging data (EEG, MEG, iEEG) shared publicly through the OpenNeuro human
neuroimaging data archive, and directly accessible for high-performance computing via the
Neuroscience Gateway. NEMAR makes possible applications to NEM data of new analysis
methods, including machine learning, to further explore human brain dynamics to gain a deeper
understanding of how the human brain supports our awareness and behavior in health and
disease. Next, we will use the NEMAR data to build new multimodal foundational deep network
models allowing user queries on relationships between brain dynamics, experience, and behavior
across datasets.

title: Domain-specific inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme as a therapeutic strategy for opioid use disorders
text:
We have discovered that inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) in the brain can counteract the
rewarding effect of fentanyl. The goal of this proposal is to develop new ways to inhibit ACE that are more
selective and specific to its function in the brain, which may lead to new treatments for opioid use disorders.

title: RNA-Protein Interactions in Nociception
text:
Over 25 million American adults live with persistent pain, contributing to their worsened health, disability and
use of health care services. New strategies are urgently needed to understand the basic mechanisms, and
develop non-opioid interventions. This project will investigate RNA-protein interactions in sensory neurons as a
mechanism for the generation of persistent pain and determine if targeting these interactions is a viable future
strategy for the development of a new class of therapeutics. Experiments will expand our basic knowledge of
how the biosynthetic machinery within pain sensing neurons responds to tissue injuries and inflammation, and
how these processes become dysregulated in pre-clinical models of chronic pain.

title: Preclinical development of breakthrough immunotherapy for brain tumors
text:
I will enhance my current research by evaluating high-risk and high-return ideas on mobilizing multiple immune
mechanisms. To this end, I will collaborate with an outstanding group of investigators whose diverse expertise
in multi-disciplinary areas complements my own in brain tumor immunology as the central component and apply
a wide variety of resources available at UCSF and collaborators to one overarching program. I will evaluate the
overarching hypothesis that the integration of novel cell-engineering and antigen-targeting approaches will allow
us to develop safer and more effective immunotherapy strategies by overcoming heterogeneous expression of
antigens and unique challenges in brain immunology.

title: C-terminal Peptide of Cardiac Troponin I for the Treatment of Diastolic Hear Failure
text:
Project Title: C-terminal Peptide of Cardiac Troponin I for the Treatment of Diastolic Heart Failure
Program Narrative
 Troponin I (TnI) regulates cardiac muscle relaxation and is a therapeutic target in diastolic heart
failure that is a clinical condition lacking effective treatment. The C-terminal 27 amino acid peptide
isolated from cardiac TnI forms a functional reagent that selectively enhances diastolic function of
cardiac muscle. Our research project investigates this myofilament-based mechanism for translational
development toward a targeted treatment of diastolic heart failure.

title: Single cell multi-omics of iPSC-derived brain organoids from patients with opioid use disorder: synthetic opioids as molecular probes
text:
Current in vitro assays and in vivo models designed to study the pathophysiology of opioid use disorder (OUD)
and to discover potential therapeutic targets are useful, but there is a need for additional model systems. Our
research strategy involves the use of induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived 3D brain organoids and
single-cell sequencing technology to identify molecular signatures for OUD using two commonly prescribed
synthetic opioids: oxycodone and fentanyl as molecular probes. This approach will make it possible to advance
our understanding of both drug action and of disease pathophysiology at the single-cell level.

title: Development of peptoid-based barcodes for in vivo high-throughput screening of targeted nucleic acid delivery
text:
There is an exponentially growing number of nanoparticles engineered to enhance the precise delivery of
genetic material to the diseased tissue for safe and effective gene therapy. The ability to cross-compare
multiple nanoparticles in a single animal offers a powerful opportunity for personalization across many
clinical applications, all while reducing the time, resources, and money in the process. The proposed project
aims to develop an effective, efficient, and enabling nano-tool for high-throughput screening of nanoparticles
in animals to assess their individual’s preferential delivery to different diseased tissues.

title: Novel roles of PCSK9 in regulating the tumor immune microenvironment during radiotherapy
text:
In this proposal, we propose to study the involvement of PCSK9, a critical protein that regulates the body’s
cholesterol levels, for its involvement in modulating the anti-tumor immune response after radiotherapy. In
particular, we will study the interaction between PCSK9 and the cGAS-STING pathway during radiotherapy and
immune checkpoint blockade therapy of local and distant tumors. Because PCSK9 inhibitors are already
available clinically for the treatment of hyperlipidemia, our study may lead to future clinical trials evaluating
PCSK9 inhibitors for their ability to improve radiotherapy and immunotherapy of locoregional and distant tumors.

title: Optimizing fluorescent nanoparticle-based motion capture to understand the neural control of movement in health and disease
text:
Movement is one of the most consequential outputs of the brain, and when this relationship breaks down, as
in the case of movement disorders, the effects are debilitating. Thus, the ability to quantify movement in the
laboratory is central to the study of neuroscience. Here we aim to advance a new technology pioneered by my
laboratory that supports motion tracking with unprecedented precision both on the surface of and inside of
laboratory animals, constituting a notable advance over existing motion tracking technologies for small
animals.

title: Dissecting the molecular mechanisms of membrane protein complex assembly
text:
Membrane proteins play crucial roles in cell physiology and are prominent drug targets, yet their biogenesis,
particularly assembly into functional complexes, remains poorly understood. Voltage-gated ion channels are
membrane protein complexes that comprise diverse subunits, regulate electrical excitability in neurons, heart,
and muscle cells, and defects in their biogenesis lead to severe human diseases. Our long-term project will
investigate how the production of functional ion channel complexes is regulated in cells and explore the
importance of the underlying regulatory mechanisms for cellular physiology and human health.

title: The interplay of social and molecular determinants in lung cancer disparity
text: The proposed research aims to provide chemokine-based patient stratification and utilize chemokines as targets for therapies, establish immune-based strategies to reduce disparities, and implement evidence-based social interventions to enhance anti-tumor immunity, thereby reducing the risk and improving the survival of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

title: 3D Bioprinted Human Model of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) Cardiomyopathy to Study Disease Progression with Imposed Force and Precise Gene Editing
text:
This project is relevant to public health because Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) heart failure is
ubiquitous and deadly, however there is a limited understanding of early disease progression due to the lack of
relevant human models resulting in no current effective treatments to prevent or limit disease progression. This
proposal is designed to allow Dr. Forum Kamdar, an early status investigator, pursue new research directions in
cardiac tissue engineering and precise gene editing through the Stephen I. Katz Early Stage
Investigator mechanism to develop a 3D DMD heart model using heart cells derived from DMD patient skin cells
to understand how the disease progresses with application of force and if these changes can be stopped by
correcting the mutation. This research is in tight alignment with NHLBI’s mission to promote the prevention
and treatment of heart diseases and enhance the health of all individuals so that they can live longer and more
fulfilling lives by identifying the early causes for DMD cardiomyopathy disease progression, test dystrophin gene
editing, and to ultimately develop effective, disease-specific treatments to prevent DMD cardiomyopathy.

title: Optical Molecular Imaging & Analysis
text: The Optical Molecular Imaging and Analysis (OMIA) shared resource provides in vivo optical imaging and spectroscopy ranging from whole animal fluorescence and bioluminescence to intravital microscopy. OMIA services can be broken down broadly according to the following categories: 1) optical imaging, 2) window chamber surgery training and support, 3) user training in techniques, and 4) scientific guidance on experimental design, data analysis and interpretation. Within optical imaging, two primary technological approaches are in vivo whole animal bioluminescence and fluorescence imaging. These are achieved using a set of commercial imaging devices, namely the IVIS Lumina and Kinetic, as well as FMT2500LX fluorescence tomography system (all from PerkinElmer). A third major technological approach within optical imaging is intravital microscopy. This approach is facilitated through resources developed over many years in the laboratory of the shared resource director. The available resources include a surgical facility and the supplies needed for performing surgeries, as well as microscopes suitable for intravital functional imaging. Together, these three optical imaging capabilities, plus the other expertise, training, and services of OMIA, provide a unique resource for DCI members to study cancer therapeutics and tumor biology. This is a vital shared resource that, in 2022, provided services to 36 DCI investigators, 73% of all users, from all 7 DCI Research Programs. DCI members benefit in particular due to the availability of cost offsets that are proportional to the DCI contribution (typically 10-30% based on the service), as well as a wide range of cancer models, which account for the majority of the utilization of these services. The impact of this facility on DCI members is best highlighted by the fact that this shared resource contributed to 22 cancer relevant publications over the project period, 6 of which were in high impact journals (Impact Factor >10), demonstrating the value of services offered by the resource.

title: Epigenetic mechanisms of positive affective state of AUD
text:
Relevance/Project Narrative
Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a debilitating disease that is estimated to cost more than $20
billion per year in health care costs and produces untold suffering. Understanding alcohol-
induced changes in the brain can lead to the development of novel therapies that can increase
the rate of successful recovery from AUD. These proposed studies will increase our
knowledge of specific brain changes caused by alcohol exposure and withdrawal and
promise to reveal novel mechanisms by which those brain changes can be reversed.

title: Biomarker Developmental Laboratory (BDL)
text: Project Summary/Abstract – Biomarker Developmental Laboratory The Biomarker Developmental Laboratory for the proposed BCC will develop and validate genomic and proteomic assays for the detection of ovarian cancer in uterine lavage samples. The genomic assays will analyze the cellular pellet from uterine lavage for genome wide hypomethylation. This genome-wide approach increases the clinical sensitivity of the biospecimen sampling. Machine learning methods will be applied to optimize the aggregation of the methylation signal across the genome accounting for the unknown fraction of sample derived from ovarian/fallopian tube cancer cells and the remaining fraction mostly comprised of uterine epithelial cells. Proteomic analysis of the uterine lavage fluid using proximity extension assays (PEAs) have a superior analytical sensitivity to mass spectrometry. Analysis of samples from a training cohort of cases and controls by PEA will identify upregulated proteins from the tumor and its microenvironment. Supervised biostatistical classifiers will define an optimal panel of up to 21 PEA biomarker proteins. The optimal panel will undergo Custom Panel development for absolute quantitation under the direction of the BRL (biomarker reference laboratory). The training samples will be re-assayed, and a classifier developed combining the custom panel proteins and the aggregated methylation signal to form a combined classifier. The combined classifier will be tested in uterine lavage samples from an independent validation cohort. If the classifier is validated, the classifier will be applied to the cervical swabs – same biospecimen as a Pap smear – to determine its performance in a readily accessible and patient acceptable sample.

title: Perineuronal nets, hippocampal plasticity, and autism spectrum disorder.
text:
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a set of neurodevelopmental conditions often associated
with social recognition deficits. Understanding the involvement of perineuronal nets, semaphorin
3A, and substance P in social recognition in healthy and genetic mouse models related to ASD
may provide clues for the creation of new therapies to restore function in development and
adulthood.

title: Identifying Electrophysiological Targets for Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Cocaine Use Disorder
text:
Cocaine use disorder is a chronic, relapsing condition with severe public health impacts and limited effective
treatment options. The current proposal aims to assess the acute effects of transcranial magnetic stimulation
on electroencephalogram markers that contribute to poor treatment outcomes and has the potential to advance
NIDA's objective of developing novel treatments that specifically target underlying neurobiological mechanisms
of cocaine use disorder. This study can potentially improve transcranial magnetic stimulation treatment and
ultimately lower the health burden of cocaine use disorder on the individual and society.

title: Unraveling Complex Disease Genetics Using Graphs and Graph Alogorithms
text: This project aims to improve our understanding of the genetic factors contributing to complex common diseases like coronary artery disease (CAD) and Type 2 diabetes (T2D) by developing novel graph-based models for genetic variation, in particular structural variants. These methods will strengthen genetic association and risk prediction studies and support future work toward improved prevention and treatment.

title: Advanced Imaging and Analysis
text:
ADVANCED IMAGING and ANALYSIS MODULE
Project Narrative
The goal of the Advanced Imaging and Analysis module is to enable visualization of cellular
dynamics of ocular tissues with unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. This innovative module
combines state-of-the-art imaging modalities with a unique, centralized resource for quantitative
image analysis and creation of visual content across presentation platforms. All our NEI R01
investigators and faculty, staff, and trainees working in vision research use these resources
extensively.

title: Cellular self-reporting: Live-cell RNA-seq with single-cell resolution
text:
Most biotechnological methods for generating complex data to understand disease, developing ideas for
treating disease, and evaluating new disease treatments require destroying (killing) cells as the first step in
analysis. This program readies an emerging new technology called cellular self-reporting that enables
advanced analyses from living cells by inducing the cells to secrete molecules for analysis so that they can be
collected without harming the cell. Cellular self-reporting enables the collection of time-series data and
follow-up analyses that are not currently possible in order to support more effective biomedical research.
